title: Why you remember faces better than names, explained.
hook: You are wired to remember faces, not names.

narration.text: You are wired to remember faces, not names.
Our brains have a special region for faces, called the fusiform face area.
This area lights up when we see a face, processing it quickly and deeply.
Names, however, are just arbitrary labels, lacking visual cues.
They are encoded differently, often with less dedicated brain power.
This means faces create a stronger, more lasting memory.
It is why you can recognise someone, but forget their name instantly.
Have you noticed this struggle in your own memory?

description: Ever wonder why faces stick in your mind, but names vanish? It is all down to how your brain processes information. We explore the specific brain region responsible for facial recognition and why it makes such a difference for memory encoding.
topic: Why you remember faces better than names, explaining the fusiform face area and memory encoding.
